name: The Pawn Breakthrough
summary: Sacrifice a pawn or two to shatter the enemy pawns and spring a passed pawn that runs to queen while the king is too far to stop it
intro: A pawn breakthrough is a sacrifice that smashes a blocked pawn chain so a passed pawn can burst through. In the diagram three white pawns on a5, b5 and c5 face three black pawns on a7, b7 and c7, and both kings are stranded on the kingside. The advanced trio looks stuck, but by giving up first the b-pawn and then the a-pawn White drags both defenders out of the way and clears a path for the third. Two pawns cost nothing next to the new queen they create.
boardCaption: White to move: three advanced pawns face Black's; 1.b6 begins a breakthrough that sacrifices pawns to send the c-pawn racing to queen.

sections.heading: What a breakthrough is
paragraphs: A pawn breakthrough is a short combination in which one or two pawns are sacrificed to force a passed pawn through an otherwise solid enemy structure. When advanced pawns face each other and neither side can make progress by pushing normally, a well-timed offer deflects the defenders off their files. The material handed over is repaid in full, and more, by the pawn that reaches the queening square.

The device belongs above all to king-and-pawn endings, where a single new queen decides the game. It works when the defending king is too far away to catch the runner once it breaks free. The key is to spot which pawn, when sacrificed, drags an enemy pawn off the file you need to open, so that your remaining pawn has a clear road home.

sections.heading: The breakthrough move by move
paragraphs: White sets the combination in motion with 1.b6, offering the middle pawn right in front of the black chain. Black removes it with 1...cxb6, and the c7-pawn has been deflected off the c-file. so the road to c8 is suddenly clear. But c6 is still covered by the pawn on b7. (If Black recaptures the other way with 1...axb6, White breaks in mirror image with 2.c6! bxc6 3.a6, and it is the a-pawn that runs.) White immediately follows with 2.a6, a second offer on the other side of the chain.

Black captures again with 2...bxa6, and the b7-pawn — the last unit covering c6 — has been dragged onto the a-file. Now the path is open: 3.c6 sends the c-pawn forward, and nothing can stop it. Both black pawns have been drawn off their files, the pawns that remain cannot reach across to block, and the king on g8 is far too distant to catch the runner. The sacrificed pawns are repaid many times over by the promotion to come.

sections.heading: How to use a breakthrough
paragraphs: Look for breakthroughs whenever you have an advanced pawn majority facing the enemy pawns and the kings are far from the action. Count the tempi: the sacrifice is only worthwhile if the resulting passer promotes before the enemy king can reach it. Work out the pawn races square by square, because a single tempo often decides whether the runner queens or is caught.

For the defender, the warning signs are advanced enemy pawns level with your own and a king too distant to help. Where you have a choice of recaptures, prefer the one that does not open a file for a passer. Above all, keep your king within the square of any pawn that might break free, so that if a breakthrough comes you can still run it down.

keyIdeas: A pawn breakthrough sacrifices material to force a passed pawn through a blocked structure.
Give up the pawn that draws an enemy pawn off the file you need to open.
The point is the new queen, not the pawns invested to make it.
Look for breakthroughs when advanced pawns face each other and the kings are far away.
In the line 1.b6 and 2.a6 deflect both black pawns so 3.c6 runs unopposed.
A pawn that cannot be stopped from queening is worth far more than the pawns sacrificed.

white: Look for the pawn sacrifice that deflects a defender off the breakthrough file.
Time the breaks so the resulting passer outruns the enemy king.
Push the freed passer straight to promotion without delay.
black: Where you can choose, avoid recapturing in a way that opens a file for a passer.
Keep your king close enough to fall inside the square of a would-be passer.
Watch advanced enemy pawn majorities for the breakthrough sacrifice before it lands.
